subject: Ellure POC: request for short-context SDK compatibility exemption and patch rollout
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Julie Park <julie@ellurehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Ellure POC kickoff + a short SDK compatibility note

Hi Julie,

Great to be moving forward — thanks for the green light on the POC for the charting assistant. We have target start next Tuesday (6/18). Before we kick off, one technical note I want to surface so we can set expectations with your engineering team: we discovered a short-context routing incompatibility in our current JS SDK when requests are under ~32 tokens and use prefetched KV caches; the runtime can route those to an optimized variant that strips session metadata, which breaks Ellure's signed-request validation.

TL;DR: this is a runtime/SDK pairing issue that only shows up for very short, high-throughput requests (what you described for on-device vitals tags). It has a safe short-term workaround (enable an "always-include-session-metadata" flag on the route) and a small runtime patch we've prepared to make the routing deterministic for these cases.

Ask: Would Ellure accept a temporary configuration exemption for the POC (we'll pin routing to non-optimized variant) that requires a runtime-side patch deployed to the POC cluster? If yes, I can loop in our runtime team and get a canary plan and timeline.

Also attaching a short excerpt from the POC logs and the proposed patch for your procurement/legal if needed.

Next steps I propose:
- Your team: confirm exemption acceptance by EOD Monday (6/17) or indicate procurement questions.
- Our side: if accepted, schedule a 2-hour maintenance window on 6/18 morning to apply patch + run canary.

Thanks,
Logan
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
--
Redwood Inference | logan.wright@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

From: Julie Park <julie@ellurehealth.com>

Logan — thanks for the heads up. We need the POC to demonstrate the tagged-vitals microfeature as-is; if the optimized variant strips metadata it will fail our signing checks. Procurement will want the patch details, but from a product POV we're ok with a temporary exemption as long as it doesn't add more than one 2-hour maintenance window and you can guarantee no data leaves our VPC.

Can your runtime team provide a short writeup of the risk and rollback plan? Procurement asked me to get a DocuSign addendum for the maintenance window and the exemption.

Julie Park
Head of Engineering, Ellure Health

Folks — forwarding thread with Ellure (Julie). They accepted a temporary exemption in principle and procurement wants a risk writeup + DocuSign addendum. High level ask from me: can runtime ship a small deterministic routing patch and an "always-include-session-metadata" route-flag we can toggle per-customer for the POC? Requirements:

- Rollback within 30 minutes if metrics indicate error spike.

Logan

Quoted message below.

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2029 14:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Ellure POC kickoff + short-context routing issue — request for exemption and canary plan

Thanks for the context — I triaged this with runtime infra this morning. Short summary:
- Root cause: variant multiplexer selects a lightweight inference path when sequence length < ~32 and KV cache hits == 0. That path intentionally omits session metadata to save tokens.
- Impact: signed-request validation fails for requests where Ellure attaches their HMAC in session metadata.

Mitigation plan (safe, minimal):
1) Feature flag: add route-level flag "preserve_session_metadata_for_short_sequences" (default off). When "ON", multiplexer will include session metadata even for optimized variant. Low-risk config change.
2) Patch: a one-file runtime patch (attached: runtime-short-context-exemption.patch) that implements the flag and a deterministic variant selection mode for pinned customers. Patch has unit tests and a small perf regression (~0.5% token throughput) only when flag is ON.
3) Canary + rollback: we'll deploy patch to staging now, then to prod-POC cluster with a 5% canary (metrics: 502/5xx, latency p95, token throughput). If metrics exceed thresholds in 15m we rollback. We can automate rollback via the release pipeline.

Operational asks of Sales Eng:
- Can you confirm the maintenance window and the exact IPs/subnets of Ellure's VPC so we can validate route isolation?
- Marissa: can you own the canary dashboard and notify Ellie if we bump the thresholds?

If you want, I can attach a draft risk writeup for procurement (1 page).

- Dev
Senior Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
